abstract: Let $S$ be the closed subspace of $L^2(0,1)$ made of step functions constant on each $(1/(m+1),1/m]$, and $V\subset S$ the closed span of the Báez-Duarte functions; let $d_N$ be the distance from $\chi_{(0,1]}$ to the span of the first $N-1$ generators. In earlier work (riemann_hypothesis_1) we proved unconditionally that $\dim S/V$ equals the number $|Z^+|$ of zeros of $\zeta$ in $\operatorname{Re}s>1/2$, identified $V$ as a jet kernel when $Z^+$ is finite, and proved a Burnol-type lower bound $\liminf(d_N^2-D_\infty^2)\log N\ge\sum m(\rho)^2|u(\rho)|^2$ over zeros on the critical line, where $u$ is the projection onto $V$ and $D_\infty=\lim d_N$. We conjectured equality. Here we prove the matching upper bound in the simple-zero case under three hypotheses: finitely many zeros off the line, all zeros on the line simple, and the Bettin–Conrey–Farmer mean-value condition $\sum_{|\gamma|\le T}|\zeta'(\rho)|^{-2}\ll T^{3/2-\delta}$. The approximants are Bettin–Conrey–Farmer mollifiers with $\mu$ replaced by the coefficients of $D/\zeta$, where $D(s)=s\,u(s)$. We show that $D$ is a Dirichlet series continuing meromorphically to $\mathbb C$, with poles only left of the line, and vanishing on $Z^+$ to the right order. The analytic inputs normally taken from RH are replaced by consequences of finitely many off-line zeros: the Lindelöf hypothesis via Backlund's criterion, a $\log^2$ bound for $\zeta'/\zeta$ near the line, and good heights for $1/\zeta$ obtained by averaging. We also derive the strip-shift heights that Bettin–Conrey–Farmer use implicitly. When there are no off-line zeros this recovers their theorem. The result refines the description of the convergence rate only; it does not bear on RH, and none of its analytic inputs uses the Euler product. A disc toy model indicates that zeros of multiplicity $m$ need the weight $(1-\log n/\log N)^m$.
author: span_of_dilates
title: Conjecture R in the simple-zero case: an upper bound for the Báez-Duarte rate when finitely many zeros are off the line
